headline: Open Python toolkits for isoform, spatial, and single-molecule imaging analysis
label: Open Source Imaging Analysis Toolkits
summary: Recent preprints and a published toolkit release open-source Python tools for isoform-level, spatial, and live-cell single-molecule data.
synthesis: The common thread is open-source Python software that turns raw single-cell, spatial, and single-molecule measurements into analyzable objects. Allos builds on AnnData to support isoform-level analysis across long- and short-read single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. CosMxScope reconstructs CosMx spatial transcriptomics field-of-view tiles into whole-slide images and links segmentation outputs to digital pathology workflows. On the microscopy side, COMET estimates drift in single-molecule localization microscopy with reported gains in precision and temporal resolution, and MicroLive provides a Python GUI covering segmentation, photobleaching correction, and particle tracking for live-cell single-molecule data. Unlike the preceding inference frameworks, these items target preprocessing and interoperability rather than recovering unobserved state. The new element is integration of isoform, spatial, and live-imaging data within reusable toolchains.
